hub.metaDescription: Give RADR operating truth. Events, files and systems become decisions.
hub.flowDecorNote: Illustrative source names only — not connection or integration status.

event.label: EVENT
event.hint: Operating signals from POS, PMS, labor, channels, and files enter normalized intake.

state.label: STATE
state.hint: Events reconcile into the Operating Model — one cross-system view of what is true now.

decision.label: DECISION
decision.hint: A Finding becomes a Decision only when material, evidenced, time-relevant, actionable, and able to change the outcome.

outcome.label: OUTCOME
outcome.hint: Prepared Actions and human choices resolve into observable results — ready to verify.

memory.label: MEMORY
memory.hint: Verified outcomes and overrides feed Operating Memory so the next decision is better informed.

finding.label: FINDING
finding.hint: A detected relationship, anomaly, exposure, opportunity or pattern — not yet a Decision.

integrations.label: Integrations
integrations.desc: Connect the systems your operation already uses.

api.label: API
api.desc: Read and write normalized RADR data.

webhooks.label: Webhooks
webhooks.desc: React to operational events as they happen.

build.label: Build your own

quickstartSteps: Create Decision when action is required
hub.quickstartFine: Sandbox key creation is not live yet. Use the proposed API design and demo reservation adapter while the platform ships.
hub.catalogLead: Status is honest. Available means a RADR path exists today. Partner access means the provider must approve before we can implement.
hub.matrixFine: Verified capability targets only, not a claim that RADR has shipped the adapter.
hub.capabilityFamiliesLead: Hotel, aparthotel, and restaurant integrations target different entity bundles. Families describe design intent — catalog status stays honest about what is shipped.

capabilityFamilies.systems: Unit PMS · channel sync · turnover · direct booking
capabilityFamilies.entities: Unit nights, orphan gaps, multi-night stays, cleaning state
Covers, menu mix, kitchen load, invoices, payouts

securityBullets: Secrets stay server-side, never in the browser or NEXT_PUBLIC_*.
Provider credentials are designed to be encrypted at rest.
Webhooks require signature verification per official docs.
API keys will support rotation and revocation when shipped.
hub.securityCert: No SOC 2, ISO 27001, or PCI certification claims are made here.
hub.dataMinBody: Prefer reservation ID, party size, time, status, table, and channel; not guest name, phone, email, or private notes.
hub.customLead: If it exposes usable data through an API, webhook, export or secure data connection, RADR can likely be designed to ingest it.
hub.previewFine: Placeholder host only. Public /v1 handlers are proposed, not production-live.

api.metaDescription: Proposed RADR public API design preview. Not production-live until handlers ship.
api.title: RADR API
api.lead: Versioned REST design for locations, operational entities, findings and ingest. Endpoints are proposed until authenticated handlers ship.
api.authBody: Server-to-server bearer key. Never put keys in NEXT_PUBLIC_*.
api.specFine: Spec and docs paths stay in English.
api.dataModelBody: Money as amountMinor + currency. Every record carries provenance.
api.advancedIngestBody: Generic event ingestion is the lower-level architecture. Typed domain methods are the approachable Quickstart path — they are not a competing product model.

webhooks.metaDescription: Inbound provider webhooks and proposed RADR outbound events.
webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.lead: Inbound provider events and outbound RADR intelligence events, always with signature verification and idempotency.
inboundSteps: Verify signature (official provider docs; raw body when required)
webhooks.inboundFine: Never invent a universal signature scheme. Never parse JSON before verification if the provider needs the raw body.
webhooks.outboundFine: Proposed schema for Technical Preview — not live delivery. Event names may change before GA.
webhooks.outboundProposed: Proposed schema — not live webhook delivery.

connectors.metaDescription: Build your own RADR connector via API, webhook, CSV, SFTP, warehouse or custom adapter.
connectors.title: Build a connector
connectors.lead: If your system exposes usable operational data, RADR can be designed to normalize it into the operating model.
connectors.contractRecommended: Recommended fields stay in English schema docs.
connectors.warehouseBody: Scoped custom implementation when needed. Authentication depends on the source — database credentials, service account, OAuth, warehouse role, access key, or signed credentials. Not one universal API_TOKEN. Prefer read-only access, restricted views, shares, or scheduled exports.
connectors.adaptersBody: Implement category adapters under the integrations adapters directory. See the adding-an-integration developer guide.

quickstart.typedMapsNote: Under the hood, typed SDK methods map to RADR’s generic ingestion / event layer.

provider.noDocs: Official documentation URL not listed. Confirm before implementation.
provider.ingestFine: Capabilities reflect reviewed provider potential, not a claim that RADR has shipped this adapter unless status is Available.
provider.authFine: Placeholders only. Secrets stay server-side, never in frontend or NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables.
provider.syncFine: Do not invent polling intervals; take limits from official docs at implementation time.
provider.implDemo: Reference adapter path stays in English.
provider.implPending: Not Available or Beta yet. RADR will not publish working provider call examples until this integration reaches Available or Beta with confirmed documentation and access.
provider.implAvailable: This integration path is Available. Use present-tense setup for the entities listed above. Limitations stay in the notes — do not invent live provider calls beyond documented access.
provider.ingestFineAvailable: Entities listed here work on this Available path today. Limitations stay in the notes.
provider.implDemoBody: RADR Demo Reservations is a RADR-provided reference data source for testing and demonstration. Use it to generate reservation events, test normalized reservation ingestion, exercise Findings / Decisions, and validate developer flows without third-party provider access. Synthetic/reference data — not a production reservation platform.
provider.implCustom: Scoped custom implementation. No generic plug-and-play adapter is currently provided. Deployment is scoped based on the customer’s systems, data model and security requirements.
provider.implPlanned: Planned — not implemented yet. Do not treat placeholders as a working integration path.

architecture.findingBody: A Finding is a detected relationship, anomaly, exposure, opportunity or pattern. A Finding becomes a Decision only when it is material, time-relevant, sufficiently evidenced, actionable, and capable of changing the outcome.
architecture.ingestNote: High-level typed SDK calls such as radr.reservations.create(...) map onto the generic event ingestion layer radr.events.ingest(...). Quickstart uses the typed path; advanced docs show the generic event API.
